node_definition.done_when: Measured at 05:34:49Z on run r-20261002T051716331338-guard-test-docstring-states-the-admitted-writes: crew resume launched attempt 2 at 05:34:47Z. Its supervisor signalled the new worker 0.3 s later with reason worker-lingered-after-terminal-manifest (the run's senders.jsonl and attempt-2-exit.json, SIGTERM). The manifest it acted on was attempt 1's complete record, written at 05:23:10Z. _supervisor_manifest_baseline_ns in reckon/crew/dispatch.py prefers the pointer's manifest_baseline_mtime_ns and uses the attempt start only when that field is absent. The supervisor's read can see a baseline older than the earlier attempt's manifest, either the dispatch-time value or a pointer read before the resume rewrote it. The fix: the delivery baseline is never earlier than the current attempt's own start (attempt_started_at from the spec or pointer, else the supervisor's own start). A manifest written before this attempt began therefore cannot count as its delivery. tests/test_a_terminal_worker_exits_within_its_grace.py gains a case through the real resume path: a stub run whose manifest reads complete is resumed with crew resume, or with the same launch the resume path uses, while its pointer still carries the dispatch-time baseline. The resumed worker is still alive after the grace, and rewriting the manifest complete then ends it within the grace. The declared negative control is executed and logged. Base and head arms of tests/test_a_terminal_worker_exits_within_its_grace.py, tests/test_stored_phase_advances.py, tests/test_supervisor_outlives_its_launcher.py and tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py show zero added failures.
